title: Arkret Circle Self-Management Operation DTOs
description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Circle administration operations (ak.self.circle.*). Every write operation carries the caller-signed ak.circle.* Event and the service submits those exact bytes through ordinary Event admission; the durable Circle object model is circle.schema.json. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md and spec/v1/zh/sync/service-http-binding.md.

circle_view.description: Circle projection row returned by create/get/lifecycle operations. Reducer-managed mls_group_id is present exactly for MLS-backed Circles; actor create payloads cannot carry it.

profile_ref.description: Create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it; profile-specific Circles expose it so clients can apply mandatory filtering.

member_count.description: Exact count of active Circle members. Present only when the caller is an active Circle member; directory-only previews MUST omit it and use the privacy-bucketed preview contract instead.

viewer_membership.description: The caller's own Circle membership state when one exists.

members.description: Active Circle member DIDs (strict subset of parent Realm.members). Empty after tombstone.

circle_create_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event and nothing else. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service cannot name the Circle and MUST NOT synthesize the Event: every actor-supplied field lives in create_event.event.payload.object, and the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md and spec/v1/zh/sync/service-http-binding.md.

create_event.description: Closed ak.circle.create Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller. Admission requires the payload closed union and forbids id/mls_group_id. The reducer derives both identifiers. encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm content-encryption floor permits plaintext.

circle_member_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event and nothing else. The target actor and the membership value live in member_event.event.payload; the Circle is payload.circle_id and MUST equal the path circle_id. The service MUST NOT add a capability verdict to the payload it submits: circle_member_state_payload is closed, and the ak.circle.member.manage decision is the admission path's, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request.

member_event.description: Closed ak.circle.member.state Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller and that payload.circle_id names the path Circle. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed by allowed_circle_ids, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member; knock requires join_rule=knock. A self-service join is gated on the Circle join_rule instead.

circle_member_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state leave Event and nothing else. The path circle_id and actor_id MUST respectively equal member_event.event.payload.circle_id and payload.actor_id; member_event.event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. The service submits the exact signed Event through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT rebuild it or synthesize a leave Event.

member_event.description: Closed ak.circle.member.state Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, with membership fixed to leave and expected_membership carrying the concrete current membership as the signed head_eq guard. Admission MUST bind the Event proof to the exact account-local lineage selected by the authenticated session; matching only the caller DID is insufficient. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to the path Circle; self-service leave uses ak.circle.member.add.

note.description: Reducer-emitted reason code on Ignored / Rejected, or unsupported-feature note while MLS scope rotation is not wired end-to-end.

circle_archive_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.archive Event and nothing else. The target Circle is lifecycle_event.event.payload.target_ref and MUST equal the path circle_id; an optional human-readable reason is payload.reason. Archive, restore and tombstone take separate request defs because each pins its own Event kind.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.circle.archive Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

circle_restore_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.restore Event and nothing else. Same shape as circle_archive_request_body with the Event kind pinned to restore.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.circle.restore Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

circle_tombstone_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.tombstone Event and nothing else. Tombstone is terminal: the lifecycle transition matrix admits no transition out of it, so the Event the caller signs is the whole record of who ended the Circle.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.circle.tombstone Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

circle_lifecycle_event_submission.description: Shared submission shape for the three Circle lifecycle Events. Its payload is object_lifecycle_payload, so the target Circle is single-sourced by target_ref. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event; admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller, that payload.target_ref names the path Circle, and that the reducer's lifecycle transition matrix admits the transition from the Circle's current state.
